timeline: The Marrucini and Frentani, allies of Rome

states.name: Campobasso

states.name: Foggia
timeline: Daunian Apulia and the Latin colony of Luceria

states.name: Barletta-Andria-Trani
timeline: Apulian towns allied to Rome

states.name: Bari
timeline: Peucetian towns allied to Rome

states.name: Brindisi
timeline: Messapians conquered in 267–266 BC; Brundisium a Latin colony from 244 BC

states.name: Lecce
timeline: Sallentini and Messapians, recently conquered

states.name: Taranto
timeline: Tarentum, surrendered in 272 BC, a naval ally that lends ships

states.name: Matera
timeline: Lucanian and Greek towns of the Gulf of Taranto

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: Bruttians of the mountains, subdued after Pyrrhus

states.name: Crotone
timeline: Croton, a Greek city allied to Rome

states.name: Catanzaro
timeline: Bruttian and Greek towns of the isthmus

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Rhegium, across the strait from Messana: Appius Claudius ferries the first legions over

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Hipponion and the Tyrrhenian coast of Bruttium

states.name: Potenza
timeline: Lucanians, allied to Rome after the war with Pyrrhus

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Paestum, a Latin colony since 273 BC, and Greek Velia, a naval ally

states.name: Naples
timeline: Neapolis, a Greek naval ally, lends ships to carry the legions to Sicily
Greek allies of the south supply rowers and sailors for the new fleet

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Capua, Rome's greatest ally, with citizenship without the vote

states.name: Latina
timeline: Latin and Volscian towns of the coast, long under Rome

states.name: Rome
timeline: Rome rules Italy through alliances but has almost no warships
Rome orders its first great fleet, copied from a wrecked Carthaginian ship
Wealthy citizens lend the money for a last fleet of two hundred ships

states.name: Viterbo
timeline: Etruscan cities; Rome sacks Volsinii in the same year the war begins

states.name: Grosseto
timeline: Southern Etruria and the Latin colony of Cosa

states.name: Livorno
timeline: Populonia, an Etruscan iron port, allied to Rome

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Lilybaeum, Drepana and Eryx: the Punic fortresses of the far west
Rome lays siege to Lilybaeum, then Drepana
Carthage crushes the Roman fleet at Drepana; Rome seizes Mount Eryx
Hamilcar holds the town of Eryx, besieged and besieging
After the Aegates, Carthage evacuates Sicily

states.name: Messina
timeline: The Mamertines of Messana, besieged by Hiero and a Carthaginian force, call on Rome
Messana is Rome's bridgehead in Sicily; the sieges are broken
Duilius wins the first Roman sea victory off Mylae
A Roman fleet beats the Carthaginians off Tyndaris

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Panormus, Carthage's chief port on the north coast
Rome captures Panormus; thousands who cannot pay ransom are enslaved
Metellus defeats Hasdrubal's elephants beneath the walls
Hamilcar Barca seizes Mount Heirkte and raids for three years
Hamilcar shifts to Eryx; the Panormus coast is Roman again

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Akragas is Carthage's main base on the south coast
Seven-month Roman siege of Akragas (Agrigentum)
Rome takes Agrigentum and sells some twenty-five thousand people into slavery
The great fleets meet off Cape Ecnomus
Carthalo raids and burns Akragas, but Carthage cannot hold it

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Phintias and Gela, allied to Carthage
The southern towns are fought over
Rome controls the south coast after Agrigentum
Junius's convoy shelters near Phintias before the storm

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Camarina, on the south-east coast, sides with Carthage
Camarina changes sides more than once
The Romans storm Camarina and enslave most of its people
A storm off Camarina wrecks the returning Roman fleet

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: King Hiero II rules Syracuse and joins Carthage against Messana
Hiero makes peace with Rome: he keeps his kingdom and pays a hundred talents
Hiero's alliance with Rome is renewed for life

states.name: Catania
timeline: Catana lies within Hiero's sphere
Catana goes over to Rome; the consul Valerius carries off its sundial

states.name: Carbonia-Iglesias
timeline: Sulci, a Punic port and mining town
A Roman fleet defeats Hannibal off Sulci; his own men crucify him
The Romans withdraw; Carthage keeps the south-west

states.name: Sassari
timeline: Punic outposts on the north-west coast

states.name: Nuoro
timeline: Mountain peoples of the interior, never fully subdued by Carthage

states.name: Olbia-Tempio
timeline: Olbia, a Punic harbour facing Italy
The consul Lucius Scipio attacks Olbia after taking Aleria in Corsica
The Roman raids end; Olbia stays Punic

states.name: Oristano
timeline: Tharros, a Phoenician port on the west coast

states.name: Medio Campidano
timeline: Punic farmland of the Campidano plain

states.name: Cagliari
timeline: Karalis, the main Punic city of Sardinia

states.name: Ogliastra
timeline: Highland clans of the east coast, outside Punic control

states.name: Enna
timeline: Henna, at the island's centre, holds a Carthaginian garrison
Dozens of inland towns waver between the two sides
After Agrigentum falls, the interior passes to Rome
Hamilcar retakes Henna by treachery
Roman armies recover Henna

states.name: Benevento
timeline: Beneventum, a Latin colony since 268 BC

states.name: Siena
timeline: Etruscan inland towns allied to Rome

states.name: Rieti
timeline: Sabine country, granted full Roman citizenship in 268 BC

states.name: Terni
timeline: Umbrian towns under Roman alliance

states.name: Perugia
timeline: Umbrian and Etruscan allies of Rome

states.name: Frosinone
timeline: Hernican and Volscian hill towns, Roman allies and citizens

states.name: Avellino
timeline: Hirpini Samnites, allies of Rome

states.name: L'Aquila
timeline: Marsi, Vestini and Aequi, Rome's mountain allies

states.name: Isernia
timeline: Pentrian Samnites of the mountains
Rome founds the Latin colony of Aesernia

events.title: Carthage rules the sea
events.text: Carthage, a Phoenician city grown rich on trade, commands the strongest navy in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: The Mamertines' appeal
events.text: Besieged in Messana, Campanian mercenaries called the Mamertines ask Rome for help.

events.title: Crossing the strait
events.text: Appius Claudius Caudex crosses to Sicily on borrowed Greek ships, the first Roman army to leave Italy.

events.title: Hiero changes sides
events.text: Hiero II of Syracuse makes peace with Rome and becomes its loyal ally for the rest of the war.

events.title: Catana's sundial
events.text: The consul Valerius Messalla takes Catana and carries its sundial home to the Forum.

events.title: Siege of Agrigentum
events.text: The Romans blockade Akragas, Carthage's base in the south, for seven months.

events.title: Agrigentum sacked
events.text: The city falls; Polybius says some twenty-five thousand inhabitants were sold as slaves.

events.title: A fleet from a wreck
events.text: Rome orders a hundred quinqueremes and twenty triremes, modelled on a Carthaginian ship run aground.

events.title: Scipio 'the Donkey'
events.text: Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio is trapped in the harbour of Lipara with seventeen ships and captured.

events.title: Battle of Mylae
events.text: Gaius Duilius uses the corvus boarding bridge to win Rome's first great sea victory.

events.title: Defeat at Thermae
events.text: Hamilcar surprises Rome's allied troops near Thermae and kills thousands.

events.title: Aleria taken
events.text: Lucius Scipio captures Aleria and carries the war to Corsica.

events.title: Raid on Olbia
events.text: Scipio attacks Olbia in Sardinia but cannot hold the island.

events.title: Hamilcar takes Henna
events.text: Carthaginian forces regain Henna and Camarina in the interior.

events.title: Battle of Sulci
events.text: Hannibal Gisco loses his fleet off Sardinia and is crucified by his own men.

events.title: Camarina stormed
events.text: Calatinus takes Camarina and sells most of its people into slavery.

events.title: Battle of Tyndaris
events.text: Regulus's fleet defeats a Carthaginian squadron off Tyndaris.

events.title: Battle of Ecnomus
events.text: Perhaps the largest sea battle of antiquity: Polybius claims about 680 ships; Rome wins.

events.title: Landing at Aspis
events.text: Regulus lands in Africa, takes the town of Aspis and plunders the farmland of Cape Bon.

events.title: Victory at Adys
events.text: Regulus routs a Carthaginian army in the hills and winters at Tunis.

events.title: Harsh peace terms
events.text: Regulus demands terms so severe that Carthage chooses to fight on.

events.title: Xanthippus
events.text: A Spartan mercenary drills Carthage's army, and its elephants and cavalry destroy Regulus's legions.

events.title: Cape Hermaeum
events.text: A Roman rescue fleet beats the Carthaginians off Cape Bon and evacuates the survivors.

events.title: Storm off Camarina
events.text: Polybius says only eighty of 364 ships survived; tens of thousands of men drowned.

events.title: Panormus captured
events.text: A rebuilt Roman fleet and army take Carthage's chief port in north Sicily.

events.title: Storm off Palinurus
events.text: Returning from a raid on Africa, the fleet loses some 150 ships off Cape Palinurus.

events.title: Lipara and Thermae
events.text: Rome takes Lipara and Thermae on the north coast.

events.title: Battle of Panormus
events.text: Metellus's troops panic Hasdrubal's elephants with missiles; over a hundred are captured.

events.title: Siege of Lilybaeum
events.text: Rome begins a siege of Carthage's western fortress that lasts until the end of the war.

events.title: Battle of Drepana
events.text: Claudius Pulcher, mocking omens, attacks and loses 93 ships: Rome's one great naval defeat.

events.title: Storm off Pachynus
events.text: A second Roman fleet under Junius is wrecked off Sicily's southern cape.

events.title: Mount Eryx seized
events.text: Junius seizes the summit and temple of Eryx above Drepana.

events.title: Hamilcar at Heirkte
events.text: Hamilcar Barca fortifies a mountain above Panormus and raids the coasts of Italy.

events.title: Hamilcar at Eryx
events.text: Hamilcar moves to the town of Eryx, trapped between Roman forces above and below.

events.title: A fleet on loan
events.text: Rome's treasury is empty; rich citizens pay for two hundred quinqueremes, to be repaid after victory.

events.title: Catulus blockades
events.text: Lutatius Catulus seizes the harbour of Drepana and trains his crews at sea.

events.title: Battle of the Aegates
events.text: On 10 March, Catulus catches a heavily laden Carthaginian relief fleet and destroys it.

events.title: Treaty of Lutatius
events.text: Carthage gives up Sicily and agrees to pay 3,200 talents of silver over ten years.

events.title: Falerii crushed
events.text: Rome turns on the rebel Falisci, destroying their city in a six-day war.

chartNote: Share of the area of the provinces on this map (today's boundaries in southern Italy, Sicily and Sardinia), by the power that held each one. It is a simplification: control often meant a few fortified towns, many dates rest on a single ancient author, and the war's real battlefield, the sea, does not appear in the shares. Mainland Italy, Roman and allied throughout, dominates the totals.
